title: promote-latest --rollback refuses a prior newer than the release (paired with quest-cli, Article 3)
description: Found by the LCLI-613 implementer while matching quest-cli QCLI-390 rules exactly (2026-09-27). Both repos --rollback checks accept a hand-edited record whose priorLatest is NEWER than the release, e.g. priorLatest "5.7.0" in a 5.6.7 record. It passes "strict X.Y.Z and differs from record.version" and "current latest is record.version or its prior" while latest still reads 5.6.7, so --rollback (not gated on a pair receipt, by design) moves latest onto an unqualified version. Fix in BOTH repos at once so the verdicts stay identical: require every priorLatest to be semver-LESS than record.version. lore implemented this once and removed it to keep parity with quest; re-add it here together with quest-cli.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore promote-latest --rollback refuses any priorLatest that is not semver-less than record.version, proven by a test with a newer prior
quest-cli mirrors the same rule, cited with both SHAs
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes: Paired with quest-cli QCLI-391 (record via opum-ai/quest-cli#317), agreed 2026-09-27, landing after the 0.11.0 pair ships. The rule: every priorLatest must compare semver-LESS than record.version, NUMERICALLY per component, so 0.10.0 > 0.9.0. The tests must include that numeric-not-lexical case, since a string comparison gets it backwards.
